title: Best Fade Haircut for Your Face Shape
content:
A great fade does more than clean up the sides. It sharpens your features, balances your face shape, and gives your whole look a more polished finish. Whether you like a low-maintenance style, a bold skin fade, or something classic and professional, choosing the right fade for your face shape makes all the difference.

At House of Handsome, our barbers understand that every client’s hair, beard, face shape, and lifestyle are different. That is why the best haircut is never one-size-fits-all. As a premium barber shop Edmonton clients trust for sharp cuts and detailed grooming, we help you find a fade that suits your natural features and personal style.

What Is a Fade Haircut?

A fade haircut gradually blends the hair from shorter on the sides and back into longer hair on top. The transition can be soft and subtle or bold and high contrast, depending on the type of fade you choose.

The most common fade styles include:

Low fade: Starts lower around the ears and neckline. Clean, subtle, and professional.

Mid fade: Starts around the middle of the sides. Balanced, modern, and versatile.

High fade: Starts higher near the temples. Bold, sharp, and more dramatic.

Skin fade: Blends down to the skin for a crisp, fresh finish.

The right fade depends on your face shape, hair texture, beard style, and how much attention you want your haircut to make.

Best Fade for a Round Face

If you have a round face, the goal is to create more structure and height. A round face usually has softer angles, so a fade can help sharpen the overall appearance.

The best choice is usually a high fade or mid fade with volume on top. Keeping the sides tight makes the face appear longer and more defined. Styles like a textured crop, quiff, pompadour, or messy fringe can add height and shape.

Avoid keeping too much bulk on the sides, as this can make the face look wider. A skilled barber can remove weight in the right areas while leaving enough length on top to style naturally.

Best Fade for an Oval Face

An oval face is one of the most versatile face shapes. It is naturally balanced, which means most fade styles work well.

A low fade, mid fade, taper fade, or skin fade can all look great on an oval face. The key is choosing a top style that matches your personality and daily routine. If you want something clean and professional, a low fade with a side part is a strong choice. If you prefer a modern look, a mid skin fade with textured hair on top works well.

Because oval faces can handle many styles, this is where your barber’s advice becomes valuable. At House of Handsome, we can recommend a fade that fits your hair type, beard, and lifestyle.

Best Fade for a Square Face

A square face has a strong jawline and defined angles. This face shape naturally works well with clean, masculine haircuts.

The best options are usually a low fade, mid fade, or classic skin fade. These styles highlight the jawline without making the haircut look too harsh. A short textured top, slick back, crew cut, or side part can all complement a square face.

If you have a beard, the fade should also work with your beard shape. A clean blend from the sideburns into the beard can make the entire look feel sharper and more intentional.

Best Fade for a Long Face

If your face is longer, the goal is to avoid adding too much extra height. A very high fade with a tall top can make the face look even longer.

A low fade or taper fade is usually the better choice. These styles keep the sides clean without creating too much vertical contrast. A textured crop, fringe, or medium-length style can help balance the face by keeping some width and movement.

For longer face shapes, it is also important not to cut the sides too aggressively unless the top is styled with balance in mind. Your barber can help keep the proportions right.

Best Fade for a Heart-Shaped Face

A heart-shaped face usually has a wider forehead and a narrower chin. The goal is to balance the upper face while keeping the haircut clean.

A low fade or soft mid fade often works best. These fades keep the sides neat without making the forehead look wider. A textured fringe, brushed-forward crop, or medium-length top can help create balance.

If you also wear a beard, adding shape around the jawline can help create a stronger lower-face appearance. Pairing the right fade with a beard trim can completely change the final result.

Why Your Barber Matters

A fade may look simple, but a great fade takes precision. The blend, hairline, neckline, sideburns, and top shape all need to work together. That is why choosing the right barber shop Edmonton residents rely on is important.

What is Precision Beard Sculpting?

Precision beard sculpting is an art form that goes beyond the traditional beard trim. While a standard trim simply shortens the beard, precision sculpting involves carefully crafting the shape and lines of your facial hair for a clean, tailored, and polished look. This technique takes into account your natural beard growth pattern, face shape, and the look you're aiming to achieve.

The difference? It’s all about the details. Barbers use tools like straight razors, clippers, and trimmers to meticulously sculpt the edges and contours of the beard, creating a look that is sharp, symmetrical, and uniquely yours.

Your barber will consider your face shape and beard growth pattern to give you the most flattering cut. Whether you're looking for a bold, chiseled jawline or a more subtle, rounded edge, precision sculpting allows for maximum customization.
  2. Longer-Lasting Results
    While traditional trims may look great right after you leave the barber shop, precision beard sculpting keeps your beard looking sharp for much longer. The precision of the trim minimizes uneven growth and gives your facial hair a clean finish that stays looking fresh between appointments.
  3. Enhanced Grooming Experience

It’s a more detailed and focused grooming session, often accompanied by a relaxing hot towel or even a beard massage, which elevates your visit to something more than just a trim—it’s a grooming ritual.
  4. Perfect for Modern Beards
    This trend is perfect for today’s modern beards. Whether you’re rocking a full, thick beard or a well-groomed goatee, precision sculpting ensures that every hair is in place and that your beard complements your style. It’s ideal for men who want to stand out with a beard that speaks volumes about their attention to detail.

We even offer additional services like hot towel treatments and beard oils to ensure your beard not only looks amazing but also feels soft and healthy.

title: The Power of the Classic Fade at House of Handsome
content:
At House of Handsome, we believe that a great haircut is more than just a style, it's a statement. One of the most enduring and popular choices in our barbershop is the classic fade. Known for its clean, sharp lines and versatility, the fade is a cut that can be customized to suit any man, no matter his style or personality. Whether you prefer a polished, professional look or a bold, edgy vibe, the fade is a cut that delivers on both fronts.

What is a Classic Fade?

The classic fade is a timeless haircut characterized by a smooth gradient of length, where the hair gradually shortens from the top down to the sides and back. This technique creates a seamless blend from longer to shorter hair, giving the cut a clean and tidy appearance. The fade can be adapted to suit any style, from a low fade that offers a subtle and refined look to a high fade that adds more contrast and drama.

What makes the fade so special is its adaptability. Whether you want a sharp, military-inspired cut or something more relaxed, the fade is incredibly flexible. It can be paired with a variety of styles on top, from a sleek pompadour to a messy, textured crop.

Why Choose a Fade?

There are many reasons why the fade remains a popular choice for men of all ages and walks of life. First and foremost, it’s incredibly versatile. The fade works for every hair type, whether you have thick, curly hair or fine, straight locks. It can be tailored to suit your face shape and personal preferences, making it an ideal option for anyone who wants a clean, stylish look with minimal maintenance.

Another reason the fade is so popular is its practicality. Unlike many other hairstyles, the fade requires little styling effort on a daily basis. With its clean, blended appearance, the fade allows you to wake up and go, without needing to spend extra time fixing your hair. This makes it a great option for busy professionals or men who prefer to keep their grooming routine simple. Plus, the fade provides a fresh, youthful appearance that is both timeless and on-trend.

How to Make the Most of Your Fade

While the fade is a low-maintenance haircut, keeping it sharp requires some attention to detail. Regular trims are essential to maintain the clean lines and well-blended fade. Our barbers at House of Handsome are experts at ensuring that the fade maintains its perfect gradient, taking the time to trim and shape it precisely every time.

Additionally, the fade is an excellent base for other styles. Want a bit of volume on top? Pair your fade with a pompadour for that classic, sophisticated look. Or, if you're after something more modern, go for a textured top or a messy quiff to create a more laid-back yet still polished style. The beauty of the fade is that it can work with virtually any style on top, allowing you to experiment and find a look that’s uniquely yours.

The sharp lines and sleek finish give you a clean, professional appearance that’s hard to beat.

At House of Handsome, we pride ourselves on delivering the perfect fade tailored to your unique features. Maintaining Your Fade: Tips and Tricks

To keep your fade looking fresh between appointments, here are a few tips to follow:

  • Use quality products: Keep your hair healthy and styled with the right products. A light pomade or styling cream works well to maintain texture and control without weighing your hair down.

  • Hydrate your scalp: To keep your hair looking shiny and healthy, make sure to hydrate your scalp regularly with nourishing oils or moisturizers.

  • Keep it clean: A clean fade is a well-maintained fade. Wash your hair regularly to avoid product build-up and ensure that the fade stays crisp and fresh.

title: How to Maintain Your Haircut Between Barbershop Visits: Tips for Men in Alberta
content:
Regular haircuts are essential for keeping your look sharp, but between your visits to the barbershop, how do you maintain that fresh style? At House of Handsome, we understand that many men want to keep their haircuts looking great without needing to come in for a trim every couple of weeks. Fortunately, with the right techniques, your haircut can last longer, looking sharp and polished even as it grows out.

Here are some expert tips on how to maintain men’s haircut between visits Alberta. These steps will help you preserve the style, shape, and overall look of your haircut until your next appointment.

1. Keep Up with Regular Touch-Ups at Home

One of the best ways to maintain your haircut is by doing a few simple touch-ups at home. A well-maintained haircut doesn’t always require professional trimming between visits. With a good pair of clippers and some practice, you can clean up edges around your neckline and sideburns. It’s best to keep the work minimal. Don’t try to reshape your cut, just clean the areas that need attention to keep your style sharp.

If you’re unsure how to do this, ask your barber for some tips at your next appointment. Most barbers are happy to show you basic maintenance steps so you can keep your cut looking fresh without overdoing it.

2. Invest in Quality Hair Products for Styling

Hair products are key to maintaining your haircut between visits. Whether you have thick, curly, or straight hair, the right styling products can help you hold the shape of your cut. For how to maintain men’s haircut between visits Alberta, consider investing in products designed for your specific hair type:

  • For thick hair: A strong-hold gel or pomade will help keep the shape intact.

  • For fine hair: Use a lightweight mousse or texturizing spray for volume without weighing it down.

  • For curly hair: A curl cream or lightweight styling gel will help define curls and maintain the shape.

Avoid using heavy products that weigh your hair down. Stick to light, flexible products that enhance your haircut's natural shape.

3. Protect Your Hair During Sleep

Your hair goes through a lot during the day, and your haircut can suffer while you sleep if you're not careful. To keep your haircut looking sharp, protect it while you sleep. Here are a few tricks:

  • Use a silk or satin pillowcase to reduce friction, which can cause frizz and disrupt the shape of your haircut.

  • For short haircuts, gently style your hair with your fingers before bed to keep it from flattening.

  • For longer hairstyles, try a loose top knot or a low ponytail to protect the shape.

While these tips may seem simple, they can extend the life of your haircut between visits.

4. Avoid Over-Washing Your Hair

Frequent washing can strip your hair of its natural oils, making it look dry and unkempt. It can also cause your haircut to lose its shape quicker. If you have facial hair that complements your haircut, maintaining it between visits is just as important as caring for your hair. Trim your beard regularly to match the clean lines of your haircut. title: Why Hair Density Matters More Than Hair Length When Choosing a Men’s Haircut
content:
When most men think about getting a haircut, the first thing they focus on is length. Short on the sides, longer on top, or something in between. What often gets overlooked is hair density, which plays a much bigger role in how a haircut looks, feels, and grows out over time.

At House of Handsome, we see this every day. Two clients can ask for the same haircut, yet end up with completely different results. The difference is rarely skill or styling. It usually comes down to density. Understanding how thick or thin your hair actually is can completely change the outcome of your haircut and how confident you feel wearing it.

Hair Density Explained Simply

Hair density refers to how many hair strands you have per square inch on your scalp. Thick hair means more strands packed closely together. Thin hair means fewer strands with more visible scalp. This is different from hair texture, which describes whether hair is straight, wavy, or curly.

Many men confuse density with length. Growing hair longer does not make it thicker. In some cases, longer hair can actually highlight thinning areas or cause hair to fall flat. This is why choosing a men’s haircut for thick and thin hair Alberta requires a different approach than simply picking a style from a photo.

Why Length Alone Can Work Against You

Length-focused haircuts often ignore how hair behaves naturally. For men with thick hair, leaving too much length without proper structure can cause bulk, heaviness, and difficulty styling. Hair may puff out at the sides or lose shape quickly.

For men with thinner hair, longer styles can expose the scalp, reduce volume, and make hair appear flatter. Instead of adding presence, extra length can remove it. This is where density-aware cutting makes all the difference.

How Thick Hair Should Be Cut

Thick hair benefits from strategic weight removal and structure. The goal is not to make hair shorter everywhere, but to control volume and allow the haircut to move naturally.

A properly designed men’s haircut for thick and thin hair Alberta takes into account where hair grows densest and where it needs relief. When done correctly, thick hair becomes easier to style, more comfortable to wear, and holds its shape longer between visits.

How Thin Hair Should Be Cut

Thin hair requires a completely different strategy. Instead of removing weight, the focus is on preserving density and creating the illusion of fullness. Clean lines, tighter shapes, and intentional length placement can dramatically improve how thin hair looks.

Blunt finishes, shorter lengths, and controlled structure help thin hair appear thicker and more balanced. This approach ensures that hair looks intentional rather than sparse, even as it grows out.

Why Consultations Matter More Than Ever

Choosing the right men’s haircut for thick and thin hair Alberta starts with a proper consultation. Density assessment allows a barber to recommend what will actually work long term, not just what looks good in the mirror that day.

At House of Handsome, consultations are built around understanding hair behavior, lifestyle, and maintenance preferences. This prevents common frustrations like haircuts that collapse after a week or styles that require constant product and effort.

Long Term Results Beat Short Term Trends

Trendy styles come and go, but hair density does not change overnight. Haircuts designed around density tend to age better, require less maintenance, and feel more natural day to day.

Men who understand their density make better grooming decisions. They stop fighting their hair and start working with it. That is when haircuts become easier, more consistent, and more confidence boosting.

Choosing the Right Barber Makes the Difference

A barber who understands density does not just cut hair shorter or longer. They shape, balance, and customize the haircut to suit the individual. This is the difference between a haircut that looks fine and one that actually fits.

If you have ever felt like a haircut looked good for a few days and then stopped working, density was likely ignored. Addressing it changes everything.

title: How to Maintain a Sharp Haircut During Alberta’s Harsh Winters
content:
Winter in Alberta can be brutal, especially for your hair. With freezing temperatures, dry air, and the constant need to wear hats, it’s easy for a fresh, sharp haircut to lose its edge. But don’t worry! At House of Handsome, we understand the challenges of maintaining a men’s haircut during Alberta’s harsh winters, and we’re here to share tips to keep you looking sharp no matter the weather.

Why Winter Affects Your Haircut

Winter presents unique challenges for your hair. The cold, dry air strips moisture from your hair and scalp, making it more prone to damage, breakage, and frizz. If your haircut has a lot of texture or volume, the winter elements can cause it to lose shape quickly. Even the simple act of wearing a hat can flatten or mess up a carefully styled look. So, how do you maintain your men’s haircut in Alberta winter without sacrificing style or health? Here are a few essential tips.

1. Keep Your Scalp Moisturized

A well-maintained scalp is key to a sharp, long-lasting haircut. The dry air of Alberta winters can cause your scalp to become dry, flaky, and irritated. To prevent this, consider using a scalp moisturizer or a mild oil like argan or jojoba oil to keep your scalp hydrated. This will also help maintain healthy hair growth, which is vital for a sharp-looking cut.

2. Adjust Your Haircare Routine

In the winter, your hair may need a different approach to washing and conditioning. Use moisturizing shampoos and conditioners to combat the dryness. Avoid washing your hair every day, as this can strip away natural oils. Instead, opt for every other day or even a few times a week, depending on your hair type. After washing, make sure to use a leave-in conditioner or light styling cream to add moisture without weighing your hair down. This will help maintain the shape of your cut throughout the day, even in the harsh winter elements.

3. Choose a Winter-Friendly Haircut

When the temperatures drop, consider opting for a low-maintenance haircut that is both practical and stylish. A haircut with clean lines and subtle fades, such as a low taper fade, works well in winter because it grows out evenly, reducing the need for frequent touch-ups. Additionally, styles that are easy to maintain, like a short textured crop or a crew cut, are great for Alberta’s cold winters because they don’t require much styling, even on the windiest days.

4. Protect Your Hair from Hats

It’s hard to escape the need for hats in Alberta winters, but wearing them can wreak havoc on your haircut. Hats can flatten your hair, disrupt the shape of your cut, and lead to unwanted static and frizz. To maintain your sharp haircut, choose hats made from breathable materials, like wool or cotton, and make sure your hat fits properly without pressing too tightly on your scalp. After removing your hat, use your fingers to rework your style. If your hair needs a little volume boost, use a light styling cream to fluff it up and restore the shape.

5. Get Regular Touch-Ups

Winter is the perfect time to keep up with regular haircuts. While your haircut might last longer between appointments due to fewer styling demands, maintaining its shape with regular trims is essential. A quick touch-up every 4–6 weeks will keep your haircut looking fresh and sharp, even when the weather is working against you.

6. Avoid Over-Styling

In the winter, it’s tempting to rely on strong-hold hair products to maintain your style. However, heavy products can build up on your hair and scalp, causing dryness and irritation. Instead, stick to light, moisturizing styling products that add volume and texture without weighing your hair down. This will ensure your haircut retains its natural shape while protecting it from winter damage.

Our expert barbers can give you the perfect haircut that not only suits your style but is also easy to maintain during Alberta’s tough winters. From winter-specific cuts to personalized haircare advice, we’re here to make sure you stay looking sharp all season long.

title: Fade Haircuts Explained: Low, Mid, High & Skin Fades What’s the Difference?
content:
When clients walk into a barbershop, the most common request we hear is:
“Can I get a fade?”
But here’s the catch, fade is a broad term, and not all fades are created equal. From low fades to high skin fades, each variation creates a totally different vibe and level of sharpness.

To help you choose the right one for your style, here’s a clear breakdown of the most popular fade types and what makes each one unique.

What Exactly Is a Fade?

A fade is a haircut where the hair gradually transitions from shorter to longer as it moves up the head. The blend should be smooth, seamless, and clean. The artistry comes from how the barber shapes that transition — this is where skill matters.

At House of Handsome, fades are one of the most requested cuts, and for good reason:

  • They’re clean

  • They’re modern

  • They work with almost any hairstyle

  • They suit all ages and hair types

But choosing which fade is right for you depends on your lifestyle, personality, and preferred level of boldness.

The Four Most Popular Types of Fades

1. Low Fade

A low fade sits just above the ear and gradually blends into the rest of the hair.

Who’s it for?

  • Guys who prefer subtle, professional, or understated styles

  • Anyone wanting clean edges without too much scalp exposure

  • Great for wavy, curly, or thicker hair

Why choose it?

A low fade adds sharpness without being too “loud.” It's perfect if you want a modern cut that still looks natural.

2. Mid Fade

The mid fade sits right between the temple area and the top of the ear — a perfect balance.

Who’s it for?

  • Anyone looking for something noticeable but not extreme

  • Ideal for textured tops, curls, slick backs, and messy hairstyles

Why choose it?

It’s one of the most versatile fades. The mid fade lets you go bold without going all-in, making it a favourite for everyday wear.

3. High Fade

This fade starts high on the head, usually around the temples or slightly above.

Who’s it for?

  • Those who want a dramatic, sharp contrast

  • Great for shorter hairstyles, textured crops, and edgy designs

  • Perfect for guys who love a clean, bold look

Why choose it?

The high fade is all about impact. It draws attention upward and creates a crisp silhouette that stands out instantly.

4. Skin Fade

A skin fade (also called a bald fade) takes the hair down to the skin at the bottom before blending upward.

Who’s it for?

  • Guys who love the freshest, cleanest look possible

  • Works well with high, mid, or low placements

  • Ideal for straight, wavy, or curly hair

Why choose it?

Nothing beats the sharpness of a skin fade. It’s clean, cool, and incredibly precise — but it does require more frequent maintenance.

How to Choose the Right Fade for You

Here are some quick tips to help guide your choice:

Consider your lifestyle

  • Professional or conservative environment: Low fade

  • Active, low-maintenance life: Mid fade

  • Bold, modern style: High fade or skin fade

Think about your hair type

  • Curly or thick hair: Low or mid fade usually blends best

  • Straight hair: High or skin fade creates a sharper contrast

Face shape matters

A good barber will adjust the fade to complement your natural features — something we always do at House of Handsome.

How Often Should You Maintain a Fade?

Fades look their best when they’re fresh. On average:

  • Skin fades: Every 1–2 weeks

  • Low/mid/high fades: Every 2–3 weeks

  • Longer tops: Maintenance depends on your style

The sharper the fade, the quicker it grows out.

Final Thoughts

A fade isn’t just a haircut, it’s a statement. Whether you prefer subtle or bold, clean or dramatic, there’s a fade that fits your style perfectly.

If you’re unsure what works best, our barbers at House of Handsome are always ready to help you choose the perfect blend.

title: The Lumberjack Beard: Tips for Growing, Grooming, and Rocking the Iconic Look
content:
The holiday season brings with it an undeniable charm, and what better way to embrace the festive spirit than by sporting a lumberjack beard? Whether you’re looking to channel your inner St. Nick for the holidays or just curious about maintaining a fuller, more majestic beard, the Lumberjack look can be both fun and stylish.  At House of Handsome, we’re here to guide you through the process of growing, grooming, and maintaining that legendary lumberjack to perfection.

1. Growing Your Beard

The foundation of a lumberjack beard is the full, thick growth that symbolizes the jolly old man’s legendary look. Here’s how you can start your journey toward growing the perfect lumberjack beard:
  • Patience is Key: A full lumberjack beard doesn’t happen overnight. It can take weeks or even months to grow, so be prepared to embrace the process. The average man may need at least two to three months to achieve a thick, full beard that resembles lumberjack iconic look.
  • Let It Grow: Resist the urge to trim too early! While trimming is essential for keeping your beard looking neat, for the full beard look, the more length you gain, the better. Let your beard grow naturally to its full potential before shaping it.
  • Healthy Beard Growth: Eating a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals, such as Vitamin B7 (biotin), Vitamin E, and zinc, can encourage healthier beard growth. Also, drinking plenty of water and maintaining good overall health will contribute to a fuller, more vibrant beard.

2. Grooming the Lumberjack Beard

Once you have a full beard, it’s time to take care of it. Proper grooming not only helps you keep the look clean and tidy but also ensures your beard stays soft, shiny, and healthy.
  • Wash and Condition Regularly: Just like the hair on your head, your beard needs regular washing to stay fresh and clean. Use a gentle beard shampoo to keep it free of dirt, oils, and product buildup. Follow up with a conditioner to keep the hair soft and manageable.
  • Beard Oil: To achieve the shiny, soft beard, apply a good-quality beard oil. This will moisturize the hair and the skin underneath, preventing dryness and itching. It also helps to tame any frizz and makes your beard appear fuller and more lustrous.
  • Combing and Brushing: Regular combing is crucial for maintaining a neat and tidy beard. Use a wide-toothed comb or a beard brush to detangle any knots and shape your beard. Combing will also help to evenly distribute beard oil or balm throughout the beard, giving it that polished look.
  • Trimming for Shape: While you want to maintain the length, trimming is essential to give your beard a clean shape. For a lumberjack beard, keep the sides fuller and let the bottom section grow a bit longer. If you’re unsure how to shape it, don’t hesitate to visit your trusted barber at House of Handsome for a professional touch.

3. The Perfect Lumberjack Beard: The Look

The classic lumberjack beard is full, bushy, and soft, making it one of the most recognizable facial hair styles in the world. Here’s how to get it right:
  • Fullness Over Everything: The key to a great lumberjack beard is volume. Unlike other beards that might be styled to look sharp and sculpted, the lumberjack beard should be soft and full. Allow the hair to grow naturally without over-trimming it.
  • The Mustache: A lumberjack beard wouldn’t be complete without the iconic mustache. Grow a mustache that blends seamlessly with your beard, keeping it a little bushier to match the full beard. You can also shape the mustache to curl up at the edges for a more playful, jolly look.
  • Soft, Not Scraggly: While you want your beard to be big and bold, avoid the scraggly look by keeping it well-maintained. Regular trimming to avoid split ends and using conditioning products ensures your beard looks healthy, even when it’s full and long.

4. Rocking the Lumberjack Beard Year-Round

While the lumberjack beard is a go-to look for the holiday season, there’s no reason you can’t embrace this beard style throughout the year. Here’s how you can wear it confidently:
  • Keep It Well-Groomed: A full beard can be a year-round statement piece, but it requires dedication. Regular maintenance and care will ensure that your lumberjack beard looks great no matter the season.
  • Embrace the Jolly Spirit: The lumberjack beard isn't just about aesthetics; it’s about embodying a sense of joy and warmth. Embrace the fun and playful nature of this iconic look, and don’t be afraid to show off your jolly side.
  • Confidence is Key: The lumberjack beard demands confidence. When you wear it, wear it proudly. It’s a sign of maturity, wisdom, and warmth, so rock it with pride!

5. When to Visit House of Handsome for a Beard Trim

Even with a beard as amazing as lumberjack, there are times when a professional trim is necessary. Here are a few signs it’s time to book an appointment with our expert barbers:
  • To Shape the Beard: If you need help with shaping the full beard or are looking to clean up the edges, our team at House of Handsome can help give your beard that perfect appearance.
  • For Beard Maintenance: Regular trims every few weeks help to maintain the health and appearance of your beard, keeping it looking fresh without losing the fullness and length you’ve worked so hard to grow.
  • For Mustache Grooming: We can also help ensure your mustache complements the full beard and doesn’t become unruly, maintaining that classic lumberjack look.

title: Mastering the Fade: A Step-by-Step Guide to Styling Your Cut
content:
A fade is one of the most versatile and popular haircuts you can get, but styling it can sometimes feel like an art. At House of Handsome, we pride ourselves on providing cuts that not only look great when you leave the chair but also give you the tools to maintain them. If you’ve recently gotten a fade or are considering it, here’s everything you need to know about styling your fade to perfection.

Understanding the Fade

Before diving into how to style a fade, let’s break down what it actually is. The fade is a haircut where the hair gradually shortens from the top down to the sides and back, creating a smooth transition. The fade can vary in length and style, from a low fade (shorter on the sides) to a high fade (starting higher up). It’s a clean, sharp cut that adds structure and dimension to any face shape.

Step 1: Start with the Right Products

The first step in styling any fade is using the right hair products. You want to avoid heavy products that weigh down your hair, as fades look best when the hair is light, airy, and well-defined. Here’s what you need:
  • Light-hold pomade or wax: For creating texture and definition without the greasy, heavy look.
  • Matte cream or gel: To add volume and hold without making it look too shiny.
  • Sea salt spray (optional): If you want to enhance texture and create a beachy, natural look.
Avoid using products that leave a lot of residue or slickness, as the goal is to maintain the sharp lines of your fade, not make it look overly styled.

Step 2: Work with Your Hair Type

The key to styling a fade lies in working with your natural hair texture. Whether you have straight, wavy, or curly hair, the way you approach styling your fade can differ:
  • For straight hair: A light, matte styling cream or paste can be used to add texture and definition. You can keep it sleek and clean or add some tousled texture for a more relaxed style.
  • For wavy hair: A sea salt spray can help enhance your natural waves while giving your fade a more natural, effortless look.
  • For curly hair: A curl cream or lightweight mousse will help keep your curls defined and controlled, while also preventing frizz. It will keep your fade looking sharp and clean, without making your curls too wild.

Step 3: Blow Dry (If Necessary)

Blow drying isn’t essential for every fade, but it can help achieve the desired volume and shape. If you want extra height or fullness on the top, blow-drying your hair in the direction you want it to fall can be a game-changer. Use a blow dryer with a diffuser (if you have curly hair) or a round brush (if you have straight or wavy hair) to add volume and control. Blow-dry the top section of your hair while gently lifting at the roots for maximum volume. Once dry, apply a light-hold product to set your style.

Step 4: Style the Top Section

The beauty of a fade lies in its versatility. The top section of your hair is where you can really get creative. You can go for a pompadour, a quiff, a comb-over, or simply keep it natural. Here’s how to style some popular top fades:
  • For a pompadour fade: Use a medium-hold product to comb the hair back and up. Focus on lifting the hair at the front while keeping the sides short. This gives the fade a bold contrast.
  • For a comb-over fade: Apply a light styling cream to the top and use a comb to style the hair to the side. A slight wave or texture can really make the fade pop.
  • For a messy, textured fade: Use a sea salt spray to add texture to the top. Scrunch your hair with your hands to add volume and shape and finish off with a light-hold wax to keep things in place without looking too polished.

Step 5: Maintain the Fade

A fade is all about maintaining sharp lines and clean transitions, so regular trims are essential. Your fade will naturally grow out over time, but it’s easy to keep it looking fresh with touch-ups every few weeks. At House of Handsome, we recommend coming in every 2–3 weeks to ensure your fade stays sharp and your style stays on point. Don’t forget to keep your fade clean by washing your hair regularly and using products that maintain its shape and texture.

Step 6: Final Touches

Once you've styled the top, it’s all about the details. Use a fine-tooth comb or your fingers to refine the edges and make sure your fade transitions smoothly. Touch up any areas where the fade might need a little more definition, and finish off with a light mist of hairspray or a touch of product to lock everything in place. Styling a fade might seem intimidating at first, but with the right products, the right tools, and the right barber, you’ll be rocking your look in no time. Whether you’re going for a clean, sharp style or something a little more textured and laid-back, your fade will always stand out.

title: How to Choose the Right Barber: A Guide from House of Handsome

When choosing a barber, experience matters. A skilled barber knows how to work with different hair types and is familiar with the latest trends and techniques. title: The Modern Slick Back: Less Gel, More Texture
content:
For years, the slick back has been synonymous with a glossy, ultra-controlled finish, think classic Hollywood charm or the unmistakable boardroom power look. But today’s version is evolving. At HOH, we’ve been seeing a major shift toward a more relaxed, textured slick back that feels contemporary, effortless, and wearable for almost anyone. This is the Modern Slick Back: still refined, still confident, but with a fresh, natural edge.

Why the Modern Slick Back Works Now

The modern styling landscape is moving toward authenticity, hair that bends with movement, embraces its natural grain, and looks lived-in rather than lacquered down. The updated slick back fits right into this moment:
  • Flexible, not rigid Less gel means hair doesn’t feel like a helmet. Instead, it maintains shape while still feeling touchable.
  • Texture is king By enhancing natural waves or adding subtle grit, the hairstyle gains dimension and character.
  • Universally flattering Whether your hair is straight, wavy, or curly, textured slick backs adapt beautifully.
  • Effort without the effort It’s intentionally styled yet appears easy, exactly the kind of aesthetic modern grooming leans into.

How to Achieve the Look?

1. Start With Clean, Damp Hair

Lightly towel-dry so hair is still pliable but not dripping. This is the ideal foundation for building controlled texture.

2. Swap Heavy Gel for Lightweight Helpers

Instead of classic gels, opt for:
  • Mousse for lift and natural hold
  • Sea salt spray for grit and separation
  • Lightweight cream or paste to guide direction without stiffness
Use just enough to support the shape, this style thrives on moderation.

3. Comb It Back, Then Break It Up

Use a wide-tooth comb or your fingers to push hair away from the face. Then, disrupt perfection slightly by raking through the top to soften the lines. This keeps the slick back modern instead of severe.

4. Blow-Dry for Shape (Optional)

A blow-dryer on low heat will help set your direction and add volume at the root. Use your fingers rather than a brush to maintain that imperfect, textured quality.

5. Finish With a Matte Product

Matte pastes, clays, or texture creams are your best friends here. They create hold without shine, allowing the natural flow and grain of your hair to stand out.

Who Does It Suit?

The modern slick back complements a wide range of face shapes and hair types. It works particularly well for:
  • People who like clean silhouettes without over-styling
  • Medium-length hair that needs direction but not control
  • Anyone wanting a style that transitions easily from day to night
It’s polished enough for professional settings yet relaxed enough for casual days.

title: The Faux Hawk: Your Ticket to Stand Out Without Going Over the Edge
content:
Looking to turn heads without committing to a full-blown mohawk? The faux hawk is the perfect answer. It’s edgy, it’s bold, and it delivers the same rebellious attitude as a mohawk, minus the shaved sides. Whether you're hitting the town for a night out or simply craving a change in your everyday look, the faux hawk offers a fresh way to express your individuality.  And trust us, when you rock this style, you won’t just be seen, you’ll be remembered. Let's dive into why this haircut is so popular and how you can rock it at House of Handsome.

What Exactly is a Faux Hawk?

At first glance, the faux hawk looks like a mohawk, but with a few key differences. While a traditional mohawk involves shaving the sides of the head, the faux hawk keeps the sides trimmed or faded, leaving the focus on the center, where the hair is styled upwards. It’s the perfect balance between daring and wearable, allowing you to experiment with your style without going too extreme. You get the same bold statement, just a little more approachable. This style isn’t just for the rebellious anymore. It’s versatile and can be worn by anyone who’s looking to add a bit of personality to their look. At House of Handsome, we specialize in making this look work for you, no matter your hair type or lifestyle.

Why Everyone’s Talking About the Faux Hawk

  1. A Style That Transcends Trends The faux hawk has stood the test of time. It’s been a popular style for years, and it’s not going anywhere anytime soon. Why? Because it’s timelessly cool and can be adapted to fit any personality. Whether you’re a professional looking for something polished or someone who loves a bit of edge, the faux hawk can be tweaked to match your vibe.
  2. Perfect for Any Hair Type Whether your hair is straight, wavy, or curly, the faux hawk works for every texture. Our expert barbers at House of Handsome know exactly how to tailor this cut to bring out the best in your hair. We’ll help you find the right balance of length, fade, and spike to suit your face shape and personal style.
  3. Less Maintenance, More Impact One of the best things about the faux hawk is that it’s relatively low-maintenance compared to a traditional mohawk. You don’t need to worry about constantly shaving the sides of your head, and regular trims are usually all that’s needed to keep the style looking fresh. It's the perfect haircut for someone who wants a bold look but doesn’t want to spend hours in the mirror.
  4. Versatile for Every Occasion Whether you’re headed to a casual hangout or an upscale event, the faux hawk can be styled to suit any occasion. A simple, sleek version of the faux hawk can add just the right amount of edge to a professional outfit, while a messier, spiked version works perfectly for a more relaxed vibe.

How to Style Your Faux Hawk Like a Pro

The best part about the faux hawk is that it’s incredibly customizable. With the right products and a little know-how, you can achieve a look that’s all your own. Here’s how to style it step by step:
  1. Start with Clean, Damp Hair Shampoo and towel-dry your hair so that it's damp but not wet. This gives you more control when styling.
  2. Choose the Right Styling Product The product you choose depends on the look you’re going for. A strong-hold gel will give you a structured, spiked effect, while a matte pomade is perfect for a more textured, natural look.
  3. Create Height and Volume Blow-dry your hair upwards using a round brush for extra volume. This is the key to achieving that “hawk” look in the center of your hair.
  4. Spike It Up Once your hair is dry, use your fingers or a comb to shape the center section of your hair into spiky peaks. The more dramatic the spikes, the bolder the look.
  5. Tidy Up the Sides The sides of the faux hawk are usually faded or trimmed short, but not shaved completely. Depending on how bold you want your look to be, you can play with different lengths for the perfect balance.
  6. Finish with Hairspray To lock the style in place, finish with a light spritz of hairspray. This will help maintain the shape of your faux hawk all day long, without making it feel crunchy or stiff.

Put Your Own Spin on the Faux Hawk

The faux hawk is all about self-expression, and the best part is, you can make it uniquely yours. Here’s how:
  • Add Color: Don’t be afraid to add some color to the mix. Whether you want a vibrant, neon shade or a subtle ombre effect, color can take your faux hawk from cool to absolutely jaw-dropping.
  • Go for Texture: If you have wavy or curly hair, embrace the natural texture and go for a more tousled, relaxed faux hawk. It’s effortless, cool, and works perfectly for casual days.
  • Shave Designs: Feeling adventurous? Shave a cool design or pattern into the sides of your faux hawk for a truly unique twist.

Ready to Rock the Faux Hawk?

The faux hawk is for anyone who’s ready to make a statement without going overboard. It’s bold, it’s fun, and it’s a look that turns heads for all the right reasons. Each of these can be tailored to your face shape, lifestyle, and personality, something we pride ourselves on perfecting at House of Handsome.

title: Essential Aftercare for Color, Bleach, and Permed Hair: Keep Your Locks Gorgeous and Healthy
content:
At House of Handsome, we know that hair transformations, whether it’s a bold color, a bleach session, or a perm, are a big deal. But the work doesn’t stop after your stylist’s chair. Maintaining your freshly colored, bleached, or permed hair requires special care to ensure it stays vibrant, healthy, and full of life. Here’s everything you need to know about aftercare for these hair treatments.

1. The First 48 Hours: Let Your Hair Settle

For all color, bleach, and perm treatments, the first two days are crucial for the health and longevity of your hair. After a color or bleach treatment, your hair’s cuticle is opened, making it more vulnerable to damage and fading. For permed hair, your hair is also adjusting to its new texture. What you should do:
  • Avoid washing your hair for the first 48 hours. This gives the cuticle time to close and lock in the color or perm. It also allows the chemicals in the perm to settle, giving your new curls or waves the best shape.
  • Don’t tie your hair up. For permed hair, avoid tight hairstyles or rubber bands that can cause breakage during the first couple of days.

2. Use the Right Shampoo and Conditioner

One of the most important steps in maintaining your newly colored, bleached, or permed hair is using the right hair care products. Standard shampoos can strip away the color or moisture, leaving your hair dull and dry. What you should do:
  • Opt for sulfate-free products. Sulfates can strip color and moisture from your hair. Choose a gentle, sulfate-free shampoo and conditioner designed for color-treated or permed hair.
  • Moisturize regularly. Bleached and permed hair tends to dry out more quickly. Look for products with nourishing ingredients like argan oil, keratin, or shea butter to help lock in moisture and add shine.

3. Keep Heat Styling to a Minimum

Color-treated, bleached, and permed hair can be more delicate than untreated hair. Excessive heat styling can cause damage, leading to breakage, split ends, and fading color. What you should do:
  • Limit heat styling. If you must use heat tools like straighteners or curling irons, make sure you apply a heat protectant spray or serum before styling.
  • Air-dry when possible. Allowing your hair to dry naturally can help maintain its strength and prevent further damage.
  • Use low heat settings. When you do style, keep your tools on the lowest heat setting to prevent unnecessary damage.
  • Use Heat Protectant. Whenever you style your hair, you must use a heat protectant to protect it from the damage.

4. Regular Deep Conditioning Treatments

After color or bleaching, your hair is likely to be more porous and prone to dryness. The chemicals used in perming also affect hair structure, leading to increased vulnerability to damage. Deep conditioning treatments are essential to replenish moisture and restore shine. What you should do:
  • Deep condition weekly. Use a moisturizing hair mask or deep conditioner at least once a week. These treatments help to hydrate and strengthen the hair, keeping it soft and manageable.
  • Add leave-in conditioners. A leave-in conditioner or serum can provide extra moisture and protection throughout the day, helping to maintain softness and shine.

5. Protect Your Hair from the Sun

Just like your skin, your hair can suffer from sun damage. UV rays can dry out color-treated hair, causing it to fade faster, while permed hair can lose its curl definition. What you should do:
  • Wear a hat or use UV protectant products. If you're going to be in the sun for extended periods, wear a hat or use hair products with UV protection to shield your hair from damage.
  • Consider products with antioxidants. Products containing antioxidants can help prevent environmental damage and preserve the health of your hair.

6. Trim Regularly to Keep Hair Healthy

Whether you have colored, bleached, or permed hair, regular trims are essential to keep your hair healthy and looking great. The ends of your hair can become dry and split over time, especially after a bleaching or perming session. What you should do:
  • Schedule regular trims. Aim for a trim every 6–8 weeks to keep your hair in top shape and remove split ends.
  • Request a trim after your treatment. After a color or bleach session, your stylist can recommend cutting off any damaged ends to ensure your hair stays healthy and vibrant.

7. Be Mindful of Chemicals in Hair Products

Certain hair products, like those with harsh chemicals or alcohol, can strip your hair of the moisture it needs, leading to dryness and breakage. What you should do:
  • Check ingredients. Look for hair care products that are free from alcohol, sulfates, and parabens. Opt for formulas that are specifically designed for your hair type, whether it’s color-treated, permed, or bleached.
  • Use products designed for your treatment. Many salons offer products that complement your specific hair treatment, ensuring your hair receives the best care possible.
Whether you're rocking a vibrant color, a bleach blonde look, or beautiful curls from a perm, maintaining your hair post-treatment is key to keeping it healthy, vibrant, and strong. By following the right aftercare steps, you can ensure your hair remains in top condition long after you leave the salon.

Facials provide a deep cleanse, removing buildup and promoting clearer, healthier skin. Exfoliation and Rejuvenation Exfoliating is essential for removing dead skin cells that accumulate on the surface. A facial exfoliates and resurfaces your skin, leaving it fresh, smooth, and rejuvenated. Regular facials encourage skin renewal, making your face appear brighter and more youthful. Targeted Skincare At House of Handsome, we offer facials that are tailored to meet your specific skin needs. Whether you’re dealing with oily skin, dry patches, or want to combat the effects of aging, our expert estheticians customize every facial to address your concerns.

2. Tips for Healthy Skin Between Facials

While facials are vital, taking care of your skin daily can help maintain the results. Here are some easy tips for keeping your skin fresh and healthy:
  • Use a Good Cleanser: Invest in a gentle, sulfate-free cleanser that suits your skin type. This helps remove dirt and oil without stripping away essential moisture, keeping your skin balanced and clear.
  • Moisturize Regularly: Whether your skin is oily or dry, everyone needs a good moisturizer. Look for one with hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid or glycerin to keep your skin plump and smooth.
  • Don’t Skip Sunscreen: Protecting your skin from harmful UV rays is essential. A daily SPF of at least 30 helps prevent premature aging, sunspots, and skin damage. Make it a habit to apply sunscreen every day, even when indoors.
  • Stay Hydrated: Hydration starts from the inside out. Drinking plenty of water throughout the day helps maintain your skin’s elasticity and glow.

Facials do more than just improve the appearance of your skin—they also offer much-needed relaxation. The soothing process helps reduce stress and tension, leaving you feeling refreshed and revitalized. When your skin looks great, it enhances your confidence, helping you face the world with a renewed sense of self-assurance.

4. Combat Shaving Irritation

Shaving can lead to irritation, razor burn, and ingrown hairs, especially if you have sensitive skin. A facial treatment before or after shaving helps prepare your skin, soothe any irritation, and reduce post-shave discomfort. The hydration and exfoliation from facials also make the skin more resilient, creating a smoother, more comfortable shave.

5. Prevent Skin Aging

As men age, it’s natural for the skin to lose elasticity, leading to wrinkles, fine lines, and age spots. Regular facials stimulate circulation, promote collagen production, and help prevent these signs of aging. By investing in facials now, you’re actively working to keep your skin firm, youthful, and vibrant for years to come. Facials aren’t just a luxury; they’re an essential step in maintaining healthy, vibrant skin. title: Perfect Skin Before and After Shaving: Skincare Tips from House of Handsome
content:
At House of Handsome, we understand that a great shave isn’t just about the razor, it’s about caring for your skin before, during, and after the process. Whether you're maintaining a clean shave or sculpting your beard, taking the time to prep and care for your skin can make all the difference. In this blog, we’re sharing expert skincare tips for the perfect shave and how House of Handsome helps you achieve smooth, healthy skin every time.

1. Pre-Shave Skin Preparation: Start with Clean Skin

Before you even think about shaving, you need to make sure your skin is clean and well-prepped. Shaving on unwashed skin can lead to clogged pores, irritation, and an uneven shave. Tip #1: Cleanse Before You Shave Start with a gentle face cleanser that suits your skin type. Washing your face with warm water helps to open up the pores and softens facial hair, making shaving easier. Use a cleanser that is free from harsh chemicals and fragrances to avoid irritation, especially if you have sensitive skin. Tip #2: Exfoliate for Smoothness Exfoliating before a shave is one of the best ways to ensure a closer, smoother shave. It helps to remove dead skin cells, which can trap hair and cause ingrown hairs. At House of Handsome, our barbers use professional exfoliating techniques to prep your skin for the perfect shave, ensuring a smooth surface for the razor to glide over.

2. The Shaving Process: Glide, Don’t Tug

Once your skin is prepped, it’s time to shave. But it’s not just about using a sharp razor—it’s about using the right products and techniques to avoid irritation. Tip #3: Use a Quality Shaving Cream or Gel Never skip shaving cream or gel. These products create a protective barrier between your skin and the razor, allowing the blade to glide smoothly over your face while keeping irritation at bay. Opt for a shaving cream with moisturizing properties to keep your skin hydrated. Tip #4: Shave with the Grain Always shave in the direction of hair growth, or “with the grain.” This reduces the risk of irritation and razor burn, which is common when you shave against the grain. At House of Handsome, our barbers are experts in ensuring that your shave is as smooth and comfortable as possible, following the natural growth pattern of your facial hair. Tip #5: Don’t Rush Shaving is not a race. Take your time, especially around delicate areas like the neck and jawline. Use light pressure when shaving, allowing the razor to do its job without pulling at the skin. Our expert barbers at House of Handsome take the time to deliver a precise, clean shave, paying attention to every detail to leave your skin looking and feeling great.

3. Post-Shave Skincare: Soothe and Protect

After shaving, your skin is more vulnerable and can be prone to dryness, irritation, and razor burn. Proper post-shave care is essential to help soothe, hydrate, and protect your skin. Tip #6: Apply Aftershave or Toner After shaving, use an alcohol-free aftershave or toner to balance your skin’s pH levels and calm any irritation. Products with natural ingredients like aloe vera, witch hazel, or chamomile are great for soothing the skin and reducing redness. Tip #7: Moisturize Moisturizing after a shave is crucial to lock in hydration and prevent dry, flaky skin. Choose a moisturizer that’s lightweight and non-comedogenic, so it doesn’t clog your pores. Our barbers at House of Handsome can recommend the best products based on your skin type, ensuring your skin feels nourished and refreshed after each shave. Tip #8: Avoid Touching Your Face After your shave, try to avoid touching your face as much as possible. Your skin is sensitive post-shave, and touching your face can transfer dirt, oil, and bacteria, leading to breakouts and irritation. Allow your skin to breathe and heal for a few hours after shaving.

From pre-shave exfoliation to the perfect post-shave treatment, we ensure your skin is well cared for. Trim any stray hairs and shape the edges to maintain your desired look until your next beard grooming session at House of Handsome.

Quick Beard Tips:

While a good haircut can last for weeks, don’t let your grooming routine fall by the wayside. Keeping your appointments every 4–6 weeks ensures your look stays fresh. In the meantime, be consistent with your grooming routine—whether it’s shaving, trimming, or styling. At House of Handsome, our barbers are happy to provide advice on how to maintain your look between visits.

Healthy hair and skin are essential for maintaining a polished look. Regular shampooing and conditioning will keep your hair healthy and free of product buildup. If you have facial hair, make sure to use a beard conditioner to keep it soft and moisturized.

title: Seasonal Hair & Beard Care: Adapting to Cold Winters & Hot Summers
content:
Your hair and beard don’t just make a style statement. They also take the brunt of every season’s extremes. Whether it’s the biting cold of Edmonton winters or the blazing heat of summer, your grooming routine needs to shift with the weather. At House of Handsome Barbershop, we know the key to staying sharp all year round is a little seasonal strategy.

❄️ Winter: Fighting Dryness & Frizz

Cold air outside plus dry heat inside is a recipe for brittle hair, flaky scalps, and static-prone beards. Here’s how to winter proof your grooming routine:
  • Hydrate, hydrate, hydrate: Use a moisturizing shampoo and conditioner to lock in moisture. Don’t over wash; 2–3 times a week is enough to prevent stripping natural oils.
  • Beard oil is your best friend: Massage a nourishing oil into your beard and skin to prevent itchiness and flaking.
  • Trim regularly: Cold weather can make split ends worse. A quick trim every 3–4 weeks keeps everything neat and healthy.
  • Cover up: Hats and scarves protect from wind damage, but opt for softer fabrics to avoid breakage and hat hair.

☀️ Summer: Controlling Sweat & Sun Damage

The summer months bring their own challenges like sweat, grease, and UV damage. Here’s how to keep it fresh under the sun:
  • Wash more often: Increase shampooing to every other day or even daily if you’re active. Sweat and product build up can clog follicles.
  • Go lighter on products: Swap heavy waxes and pomades for lightweight creams or sea salt sprays for a natural look.
  • UV protection matters: Use a leave-in conditioner with UV filters or wear a cap when spending long hours outside.
  • Keep your beard fresh: Wash your beard daily with a gentle cleanser and use a light oil or balm to keep it soft without feeling greasy.

🧴 Year Round Essentials

No matter the season, these habits keep your hair and beard game strong:
  • Stay hydrated: Healthy hair starts from within. Drink plenty of water.
  • Eat well: Protein, omega 3s, and vitamins support hair growth and strength.
  • Book consistent appointments: Regular cuts every 3–5 weeks keep your style in shape, whether you’re rocking a fade, a pompadour, or a full beard.

title: The Beard Breakdown: What Style Suits You Best?
content:
The best beard styles for men can completely transform your look, highlighting your features and showcasing your personality. But with so many styles to choose from, how do you know which one suits you best? Whether you prefer a classic, clean-cut look or a bold, rugged vibe, finding the right beard style starts with understanding your face shape and grooming preferences. In this guide, we’ll break down popular beard styles and help you discover the one that’s perfect for you.  

The Classic Stubble

If you’re looking for low-maintenance yet effortlessly stylish facial hair, the classic stubble is perfect. It works well for most face shapes, adds a touch of rugged charm, and doesn’t require significant upkeep—just regular trimming to keep it sharp.  

The Corporate Beard

For a professional, polished look, the corporate beard strikes the right balance. This medium-length beard style is perfect for those who want a distinguished appearance without veering into overly bold territory. It pairs well with square and oval face shapes.  

The Full Beard

Bold and timeless, the full beard is ideal for those who want to make a strong style statement. It works best for men with oval or rectangular face shapes and thicker hair. Keeping it well-shaped and trimmed is essential for avoiding an unkempt look.  

The Goatee

The goatee is a versatile choice that can be adapted in several ways, from the classic chin-only style to combinations with a mustache. This beard style suits rounder face shapes by elongating the appearance of the chin.  

The Van Dyke

For a touch of vintage sophistication, the Van Dyke combines a pointed goatee and a separate mustache. It’s a great option for angular face shapes and those who like a more artistic or unique look.  

Choosing the Right Beard for You

To find the best beard styles for men, start by considering your face shape. Oval faces work with nearly all styles, while rounder faces benefit from styles that add length, like the goatee. Square and rectangular faces shine with styles that soften sharp angles, such as a full or corporate beard. Once you’ve identified the style you want, it’s crucial to maintain it with regular trims, proper grooming products, and care tailored to your beard type.

title: Low Taper Fade: A Timeless Look for Every Gentleman
content:
The low taper fade is a classic haircut that has stood the test of time, offering a refined look that suits any occasion. With its clean lines and subtle transitions, this style perfectly balances sophistication and ease, making it a favorite among men of all ages. Whether you're dressing up for a formal event or just keeping it casual, the low taper fade adapts effortlessly. In this blog, we’ll dive into why this cut is so popular, how to keep it looking sharp, and what makes it the ideal choice for the modern gentleman looking to make a statement.
How to Style a Low Taper Fade
Styling a low taper fade is all about enhancing the natural flow of your hair while keeping things low-maintenance. Here are some simple styling tips: Choose a Length That Suits You: The beauty of the low taper fade is that it pairs well with almost any length on top. If you prefer a longer look, you can go for a classic pompadour or loose, textured style. For a cleaner, shorter look, keep the top close-cropped, which complements the fade’s gradual blend. Use the Right Products: The low taper fade looks best with a bit of styling product to define the shape and add polish. For thicker hair, a matte clay or pomade helps hold the style without making it stiff. For thinner hair, a lightweight mousse or gel can add volume and definition. Comb or Brush for Definition: A quick comb-through or brush-up helps create a well-defined look. For shorter styles, use a comb to maintain a sleek, close-to-the-head appearance. For longer styles, a brush can help achieve a softer, more voluminous effect. Add Texture for a Modern Look: If you want a contemporary twist, work in some texture by using your fingers to tousle the top layers. This creates a relaxed, effortless feel that pairs beautifully with the fade’s clean lines.  
Maintenance Tips for a Sharp Look
The low taper fade requires minimal upkeep, but regular maintenance is key to keeping it looking fresh. Here’s how to keep your fade sharp between cuts: Visit the Barbershop Every 2–4 Weeks: Because the fade gradually grows out, a visit to the barbershop every few weeks keeps the look crisp. Your barber will clean up the sides, trim the neckline, and reshape the top to maintain your style. Daily Care with Minimal Effort: Washing with a gentle shampoo and conditioner every few days keeps your hair healthy without stripping it of natural oils. A light spritz of leave-in conditioner or styling spray can add moisture and a touch of shine. Protect Against Frizz and Flyaways: A bit of styling cream or anti-frizz serum keeps everything smooth, especially in humid weather. It also helps keep your hair looking polished and in place all day.  
Why the Low Taper Fade is a Timeless Choice
The low taper fade is timeless because it adapts to any trend, lifestyle, and personal taste. It’s professional enough for the office, stylish enough for nights out, and easy enough to maintain daily. This versatility is one reason why so many men choose this cut and stick with it year after year. Whether you’re new to the fade or looking to try a more subtle variation, the low taper fade offers a balanced, stylish look that never goes out of fashion.

title: Fade Haircuts for Every Face Shape: Our Expert Tips
content:
Finding the right fade haircut can be a game-changer, but did you know that the best fade for you depends largely on your face shape? At House of Handsome, we believe every client deserves a fade that highlights their unique features and enhances their personal style. Whether you’ve got a square jawline, rounder contours, or a long face shape, choosing the right fade can make all the difference. What is a Fade Haircut? A fade haircut is characterized by a gradual blending of hair length, creating a seamless transition from short to longer hair. Fades are versatile and can be adjusted in length, placement, and blending style to suit individual preferences and face shapes. The three most common types are the low fade, mid fade, and high fade, each offering a unique way to frame the face and create balance. Determining Your Face Shape Before choosing a fade, it’s helpful to determine your face shape. Here’s a quick guide: Oval: Your face length is greater than the width of the cheekbones, with a rounded jawline. Square: You have a sharp jawline and your face is as wide as it is long. Round: The width of your face is similar to its length, with soft, rounded edges. Oblong (or Rectangle): Your face is longer than it is wide, with a straighter jawline. Diamond: You have a narrow forehead and jawline, with prominent cheekbones. Once you know your face shape, finding a fade style that enhances it becomes easier. Fade Haircuts for Each Face Shape
  1. Oval Face Shape
An oval face shape is incredibly versatile, and almost any fade style will work well. The balanced proportions of an oval face make it easy to experiment, so you can try low, mid, or high fades without worry. Here are some tips to keep in mind: Recommendation: Try a mid-fade paired with a textured top for a modern, balanced look. Why It Works: A mid fade accentuates an oval face’s symmetry and keeps the focus on your overall style rather than any specific feature.
  1. Square Face Shape
Square faces have strong, angular jawlines that can handle a bold cut. A high fade is an excellent option, as it emphasizes the face's structure and draws attention to the jawline. Recommendation: Go for a high fade with a short crop or buzz cut on top. Why It Works: The high fade sharpens your look and highlights your naturally chiseled features, making the square face shape appear even more defined.
  1. Round Face Shape
A round face benefits from hairstyles that add height and structure, creating the illusion of a longer face. Opt for a high or mid fade with volume on top to balance the softness of a round face. Recommendation: Try a high fade with a pompadour, quiff, or spiky top to add length. Why It Works: The height on top contrasts with the roundness of the face, elongating it and adding structure to the overall shape.
  1. Oblong Face Shape
For an oblong or rectangular face, the key is to avoid adding extra height on top, which can make the face appear even longer. A low or mid fade with a more subtle style on top works well here. Recommendation: Choose a low fade paired with a crew cut or side-swept style. Why It Works: A low fade minimizes the vertical emphasis, keeping the style balanced and proportionate to the longer face shape.
  1. Diamond Face Shape
A diamond face shape, with its narrow forehead and jawline and broader cheekbones, can handle some drama up top. A low or mid fade with added width on the sides complements this shape well. Recommendation: Go for a mid-fade with textured layers on top, or a faux hawk to play up the cheekbones. Why It Works: The mid fade balances out the cheekbones and draws attention to the eyes, creating a proportionate look that highlights the unique diamond shape.   Maintenance Tips for Your Fade Haircut No matter your fade style, regular upkeep is key to keeping it looking sharp: Schedule Regular Trims: To maintain clean lines and the ideal length, a fade typically needs a touch-up every two to three weeks. Use Quality Hair Products: Styling creams, pomades, or texturizing sprays can help you achieve the volume or texture that complements your face shape. Protect Your Hair and Scalp: Since fades involve shorter hair, your scalp may be more exposed. Consider using SPF or a moisturizing product to keep it healthy.   Why a Fade is Worth the Upgrade A fade haircut does more than just look sharp—it’s adaptable, timeless, and can be customized to your unique style and face shape. Whether you’re after a subtle, low-key look or something bold and edgy, House of Handsome is here to help you find the fade that makes you look your best.   Ready to try the fade that’s right for your face shape? At House of Handsome, our barbers specialize in tailoring fades to each individual, ensuring you leave with a haircut that’s both stylish and suited to you. Book your appointment today and let us help you find the perfect fade!

title: How To Style a Buzzcut for Every Occasion
content:
The buzzcut is more than just a low-maintenance haircut—it’s a versatile style that can be adapted for any occasion. Whether you’re headed to a casual day out or suiting up for a formal event, your buzzcut can always look sharp with the right styling tips. In this guide, we’ll walk you through how to style your buzzcut to suit every moment, ensuring you stay fresh, confident, and on point no matter where you’re going.  
  1. Casual Day Out: The Effortless Look
For those laid-back days when you want a simple yet clean appearance, your buzzcut is the perfect low-maintenance solution. All you need is a bit of texture and a natural finish to give your buzzcut a relaxed vibe. Here’s how to achieve it: Step 1: Apply a small amount of lightweight styling cream or pomade to damp hair. Step 2: Use your fingers to distribute the product evenly, giving it a slightly messy look. Step 3: Let your hair air dry for a natural, effortless style.  
  1. Office-Ready: The Polished Professional
Even with a buzzcut, you can maintain a sharp and professional appearance that’s perfect for the workplace. The key here is precision and neatness: Step 1: Start with freshly washed hair and towel dry it. Step 2: Use a small amount of matte styling gel or wax to keep your hair looking neat without the shine. Step 3: Apply the product evenly and use a comb to smooth out any stray hairs, ensuring a clean, professional finish.  
  1. Date Night: The Subtle Statement
For a romantic evening out, your buzzcut can still make a big impact. The goal here is to add a bit of edge while keeping it sleek and suave: Step 1: Use a moisturizing cream or light pomade to hydrate your scalp and give your buzzcut a subtle shine. Step 2: Lightly comb or brush your hair in the direction it naturally grows to create a smooth, even surface. Step 3: For extra style points, pair your buzzcut with a well-groomed beard or facial hair for a bold yet sophisticated look.  
  1. Special Events: The Red-Carpet Look
Whether it’s a wedding, gala, or black-tie event, a buzzcut can be the ultimate formal hairstyle with the right preparation. The goal here is sleekness and shine: Step 1: Apply a nourishing scalp oil or light pomade to add some shine and ensure your scalp looks healthy and hydrated. Step 2: Use a fine-tooth comb to smooth out your buzzcut, ensuring every hair is in place. Step 3: Finish with a light mist of shine spray for that extra polished, camera-ready look.  
  1. Weekend Getaway: The No-Fuss Look
If you’re off on a weekend adventure, your buzzcut is the perfect travel companion—it requires minimal effort and looks good no matter what. Here’s how to keep it looking sharp: Step 1: Pack a small bottle of leave-in conditioner or a hair oil to maintain hydration. Step 2: Bring a lightweight styling balm to add a bit of control if needed. Step 3: Let your hair dry naturally, enjoying the fact that your buzzcut will stay fuss-free the entire trip.   The beauty of a buzzcut is in its simplicity and versatility. With just a few adjustments and the right products, you can tailor your buzzcut to any occasion, from casual hangouts to formal events. By keeping your hair well-maintained and adding subtle touches for each situation, your buzzcut can make a statement wherever you go.   Ready to perfect your buzzcut?
