title: Cool and Easy Men’s Hairstyles for a Hot Summer
content:
Summer is here, and with it comes the need for hairstyles that not only look great but also keep you cool and comfortable. Whether you're hitting the beach, attending a backyard barbecue, or just trying to survive the heat, having the right hairstyle and hair maintenance can make all the difference. We will be exploring a range of cool and easy men’s hairstyles perfect for the hot summer months. From trendy cuts to timeless classics, these styles will help you stay fresh and stylish, no matter how high the temperature climbs. So, let’s find the perfect summer look for you!  
  1. The Buzz Cut
The buzz cut is the ultimate low-maintenance hairstyle. It's easy to achieve, requires minimal upkeep, and is perfect for keeping cool. The close-cropped style reduces the amount of hair on your head, making it an ideal choice for hot weather. Plus, it's a timeless classic that never goes out of style.
  1. The Crew Cut
Similar to the buzz cut but with a bit more length on top, the crew cut is another fantastic summer hairstyle. It provides a clean, sharp look while still being easy to manage. The slightly longer hair on top can be styled with a bit of product, giving you versatility without sacrificing comfort.
  1. The Short Pompadour
For those who want a bit more flair, the short pompadour is a stylish option. This cut keeps the sides and back short while leaving more length on top to create volume. With the right products, you can achieve a sleek, polished look that holds up even in the summer heat.
  1. The Undercut
The undercut remains a popular choice for men of all ages. This style features short or shaved sides with longer hair on top, allowing for a variety of styling options. Whether you prefer a slicked-back look or a more relaxed, textured finish, the undercut provides a cool and contemporary look that’s perfect for summer.
  1. The Textured Crop
The textured crop is a great option for those who prefer a more relaxed, tousled appearance. This style involves short to medium-length hair on top with lots of layers to add texture and movement. It’s an easygoing look that can be styled with minimal effort, making it perfect for casual summer days.
  1. The Fade
The fade is a versatile and trendy haircut that works well in hot weather. This style involves gradually tapering the hair from short to shorter, creating a clean and seamless look. Whether you choose a high, mid, or low fade, this cut can be combined with various styles on top, from crops to pompadours.   Tips for Maintaining Your Summer Hairstyle From protecting your locks from sun damage to choosing the right products for a lightweight hold, there are several strategies to ensure your hair stays in top. There are some essential tips for maintaining your summer hairstyle so you can enjoy the season with confidence and flair. Whether you have short, long, curly, or straight hair, these practical tips will help you navigate the challenges of summer hair care with ease. Use Lightweight Products: Opt for lightweight styling products that won’t weigh your hair down or make it feel greasy in the heat. Stay Hydrated: Keeping your body hydrated helps maintain healthy hair. Drink plenty of water to keep your hair and scalp moisturized. Regular Trims: Regular trims help keep your hairstyle looking fresh and prevent your hair from becoming too unruly in the heat. Protect from the Sun: Use a hat or a leave-in conditioner with SPF to protect your hair from sun damage.   With these cool and easy men’s hairstyles, you’ll be ready to take on summer with style and confidence. Whether you prefer a clean-cut look or something more relaxed, there’s a perfect summer hairstyle out there for you. So, book your appointment to House of Handsome, get your summer cut, and enjoy the season looking your best!

title: The Evolution of Men's Grooming: From Tradition to Trendsetting
content:
Men's grooming has experienced a remarkable transformation, transitioning from age-old practices rooted in tradition to a contemporary industry fueled by innovation and personal expression. In this blog, we will explore the fascinating journey of men's grooming, highlighting how historical customs have influenced modern trends and how current advancements are paving the way for the future. Join us as we dive into the past, present, and future of grooming, celebrating the timeless rituals and cutting-edge developments that shape this ever-changing landscape.
Early Days: Simple Beginnings
In the early 20th century, men's grooming was a straightforward affair. Basic tools like razors, shaving brushes, and simple soaps were the norm. These products were functional, serving the purpose of keeping men looking neat and presentable.
The Rise of Specialization
As society evolved, so did men's grooming needs. The mid-20th century saw the rise of specialized products catering to specific aspects of grooming. Hair styling became more refined with the introduction of pomades and hair creams, offering men the ability to sculpt and shape their hair into fashionable styles.
The Modern Renaissance
Fast forward to today, men's grooming has entered a renaissance of sorts. The market is flooded with a plethora of products designed to cater to every conceivable grooming need. From beard oils and balms that nourish and tame facial hair to sophisticated skincare regimens tailored to men's unique skin concerns, the options are endless. Men often use female skincare products up until now, but recently a brand called Atwater turned the tables upside down when CEO Chris Salgardo, former president of skincare megabrand Kiehl's, mentioned in a Mountains Media interview that "women often inquire if our products are suitable for them as well and the answer is a resounding 'yes.'"
Technology Meets Tradition
One of the most exciting aspects of the current grooming landscape is the fusion of traditional techniques with cutting-edge technology. Electric shavers and trimmers have revolutionized the shaving experience, offering convenience without sacrificing precision. At the same time, artisanal products crafted with natural ingredients harken back to a time when craftsmanship and quality were dominant.
The Role of Barber Shops
In this age of abundance, barber shops like House of Handsome play a crucial role. Beyond offering top-notch grooming services, we serve as educators, guiding men to navigate through the vast array of products to find what suits their unique needs best. Whether it's recommending the perfect pomade for a classic look or advising on a skincare routine tailored to specific concerns, barbers are trusted advisors in the quest for personal style and grooming excellence.
Looking Ahead: Trends and Innovations
As we look to the future, the evolution of men's grooming shows no signs of slowing down. We can expect advancements in sustainable packaging, cruelty-free formulations, and personalized grooming solutions. The emphasis on self-care and grooming as an essential part of overall well-being continues to grow, making it an exciting time for the grooming industry. Whether you're a seasoned grooming enthusiast or just beginning your journey, we're here to guide you with expert advice and premium services. title: The Science of Beard Growth: How Trimming Affects Your Beard
content:
Growing a beard is more than just a fashion statement; it's a journey that involves understanding the intricacies of facial hair. Whether you're aiming for a rugged look or a neatly groomed beard, the science behind beard growth and the impact of trimming are essential to achieving your desired style. In this blog, we delve into how trimming influences beard growth and overall beard health.  

The Role of Trimming in Beard Growth

Contrary to popular belief, trimming your beard does not directly affect the speed of hair growth. Hair growth is governed by the follicles beneath your skin, which are unaffected by surface-level trimming. However, regular trimming plays a crucial role in maintaining the health and appearance of your beard:   Preventing Split Ends: Just like the hair on your head, beard hair can develop split ends. Trimming helps remove these damaged ends, preventing further splitting and ensuring your beard remains healthy and strong. Shaping and Style Maintenance: Regular trims help you maintain the desired shape and style of your beard. Whether you prefer a well-defined jawline or a more natural look, trimming allows you to control the growth pattern and overall appearance. Promoting Even Growth: Trimming can help manage uneven growth by encouraging slower-growing areas to catch up with faster-growing ones. This results in a fuller and more uniform beard. Reducing Itchiness and Irritation: As your beard grows, it can cause itchiness and skin irritation. Trimming helps keep the length manageable and reduces the likelihood of these discomforts. Hygiene: Keeping your beard trimmed and well-groomed promotes better hygiene. It’s easier to clean and less likely to trap food particles and bacteria.   Trimming is an essential aspect of beard care that significantly influences the health and appearance of your facial hair. While it doesn't directly speed up hair growth, it prevents damage, promotes even growth, and helps you maintain your desired style. Understanding the science behind beard growth and implementing effective trimming practices can help you achieve a healthy, stylish, and well-maintained beard.   Ready to take your beard to the next level? title: Embrace The Retro Look: Join The Comeback Of Mullet For A Modern Style
content: Here in House Of Handsome, we always explore the ever-evolving world of men’s grooming and style. Throughout the recent years, we’ve seen a lot of retro-inspired looks resurface the fashion trends, and one style that is getting a momentous comeback is the famous mullet cut. It was once the go-to style to show a bold and rebellious spirit in the ‘80s, and is once again getting its place in the spotlight as a versatile and in vogue option for the modern men who like to express their personality. Let’s delve more into the resurgence of this famous hairstyle, exploring how it’s being reimagined for the summer season and why it’s been capturing the eyes of fashion-forward men. Get ready to discover why this daring ‘do is reclaiming its spot as a style staple.   The Mullet: A Brief History The mullet is deeply rooted in the cultural landscape of the ‘80s. With its signature short front and sides, and longer locks at the back added, the mullet became the symbol of rebellion and nonconformity. From rockstars to athletes, the mullet was embraced by icons who tried to challenge traditional norms and express their individuality through their hairstyle. The Mullet’s Modern Makeover Skipping to today, the mullet is going through a modern makeover that’s breathing new life into the classic style. Gone are the overly-dramatic and exaggerated varieties of the past. Instead, contemporary mullets feature subtle versions that hit the perfect balance between retro charm and modern sophistication. With shorter, more tailored layers in the front complemented by textured lengths at the back, today’s mullet is sleek, stylish and effortlessly cool. Why The Mullet Matters So, what’s the cause of the comeback of the mullet in today’s fashion trends? title: The Art of the Shave: Traditional vs. Hot Towel Techniques at House of Handsome Barbershop
content:
At House of Handsome Barbershop, we celebrate the ritual of shaving by offering both traditional and modern experiences, with a special emphasis on the luxurious hot towel shave. Here, we explore the nuances of traditional wet shaving compared to the indulgent hot towel shave, highlighting their unique tools, techniques, and skincare benefits.

Traditional Wet Shaving: A Timeless Practice

Traditional wet shaving is a classic method revered for its precision and connection to the grooming rituals of the past. It typically involves the use of a straight razor or safety razor, a quality shaving brush, and traditional shaving cream or soap.
  • Tools: The straight razor, celebrated for its single blade, offers unmatched precision. The safety razor provides a safer but equally effective alternative. The shaving brush is essential for creating a rich, protective lather.
  • Technique: This method requires skill and patience, as the razor glides over the skin, providing a close and clean shave.
  • Skin Care: Traditional wet shaving can be gentler on the skin, minimizing razor burn and irritation. Natural soaps and aftershaves soothe and protect the skin, enhancing the shaving experience.

Hot Towel Shave: The Modern Indulgence

The hot towel shave, a modern twist on the traditional shave, combines the luxury of warmth and relaxation with the precision of professional shaving techniques.
  • Tools: This method also uses a straight or safety razor. The highlight, however, is the application of hot towels, which are used to soften the beard and open up pores, preparing the skin for a closer shave.
  • Technique: The hot towel is applied before the shave to soften the beard and again after shaving to cleanse and soothe the skin. This method not only ensures a closer shave but also turns the experience into a spa-like treatment.
  • Skin Care: The warmth from the hot towels promotes blood circulation, enhancing skin health and relaxation. Combined with premium shaving creams and soothing aftershaves, the hot towel shave is a luxurious experience that pampers the skin.

Experience the Best of Both Worlds at House of Handsome

Whether you prefer the classic touch of traditional wet shaving or the modern luxury of a hot towel shave, House of Handsome Barbershop is here to provide an exceptional experience. Our expert barbers are skilled in both techniques, ensuring that you receive a shave that’s not only about looking good but also about feeling great.

Immerse yourself in the art of the shave at House of Handsome. Book an appointment with us and choose between the timeless elegance of traditional wet shaving or the soothing luxury of a hot towel shave. Join us for a shave and discover how this quintessential grooming ritual can be a highlight of your routine–combining care, precision, and relaxation.

title: What is Beard Balm and How Do You Use It?
content:
Beard balm has become a staple in the grooming routine of men who take their beard care seriously. At House of Handsome Barbershop, we understand the importance of a well-maintained beard, and we're here to guide you through the ins and outs of using beard balm effectively.

What is Beard Balm?

Beard balm is a leave-in conditioner that not only helps to moisturize and soften your beard but also provides styling and control. It typically contains a blend of natural butters (like shea or cocoa), beeswax, and carrier oils (such as jojoba or argan oil), often enhanced with essential oils for fragrance.

Why Use Beard Balm?

  • Moisturization: Beard balm hydrates the beard and the skin underneath, preventing dryness and itchiness.
  • Styling: Its slight hold helps to tame unruly hairs and shape your beard.
  • Softening: Regular use of beard balm can make your beard feel softer and more manageable.
  • Health: The natural ingredients often found in beard balms promote overall beard health and growth.

How to Use Beard Balm Effectively

  1. Start with a Clean Beard: Apply beard balm after washing your beard with a mild beard wash. Pat your beard dry as applying balm to a damp (not wet) beard is most effective.
  2. Scoop Out the Right Amount: Depending on the length and thickness of your beard, scoop out a small amount of beard balm with the back of your thumbnail. A little goes a long way.
  3. Emulsify the Balm: Rub the balm between your palms to warm and soften it. This makes it easier to apply and ensures even distribution.
  4. Apply Thoroughly: Work the balm into your beard, starting from the roots and moving to the tips. Make sure to massage it into the skin underneath your beard as well.
  5. Style as Desired: Use your fingers or a beard comb to style your beard to your liking. The balm will provide a light hold to keep your beard looking neat.
  6. Regular Use: For best results, use beard balm daily as part of your grooming routine.

Choosing the Right Beard Balm for You

  • Ingredient Quality: Look for natural ingredients and avoid balms with artificial fragrances or colors.
  • Hold and Shine: Different balms offer varying levels of hold and shine. Choose one that matches your styling needs.
  • Scent: Select a scent that you enjoy, as it will be noticeable throughout the day.

Visit House of Handsome for Personalized Advice

Every beard is unique, and so are your grooming needs. At House of Handsome Barbershop, our experts are ready to help you choose the right beard balm and provide personalized tips for your beard type and style. Remember, a great beard doesn't happen overnight, but with the right tools and care, including the use of beard balm, you're well on your way to achieving a handsome, healthy beard. Drop by House of Handsome Barbershop for more beard care tips and tricks, and let us help you keep your beard in prime condition year-round.

title: Winter Beard Care: Keeping Your Beard Hydrated and Healthy
content:
As the winter season sets in, the cold, harsh weather can take a toll on your beard. At House of Handsome Barbershop, we understand the importance of maintaining a healthy and hydrated beard during these colder months. In this blog, we'll share some essential tips to keep your beard looking its best, even in the chill of winter.
  1. Understand the Impact of Winter on Your Beard Winter weather, characterized by cold air and harsh winds, can strip moisture from your beard, leading to dryness, itchiness, and flakiness. Indoor heating can further exacerbate the problem by reducing humidity levels.
  2. Keep It Clean, But Don't Overwash Regular washing is crucial, but overwashing your beard in winter can strip away natural oils. We recommend using a mild, moisturizing beard wash 2-3 times a week.
  3. Invest in Quality Beard Oil Beard oil is a winter essential. It not only replenishes moisture but also nourishes the skin underneath. Look for oils with natural ingredients like jojoba, argan, or coconut oil. Apply it daily after showering to lock in moisture.
  4. Don't Skip the Beard Balm Beard balm acts as a leave-in conditioner that not only moisturizes but also provides a protective layer against the cold. It's perfect for longer beards that need extra care.
  5. Hydration From the Inside Out Staying hydrated isn’t just about what you put on your beard. Drinking plenty of water is vital for overall skin and beard health, especially in winter.
  6. Regular Trimming is Key Trimming your beard regularly helps get rid of split ends and promotes healthy growth. You don’t have to do it yourself; our skilled barbers at House of Handsome are here to help.
  7. Use a Beard Brush or Comb A natural bristle beard brush or a wide-toothed comb is ideal for maintaining your beard. It helps distribute oils evenly, stimulates the skin, and keeps your beard neat.
  8. Protect Your Beard from the Elements When stepping out in cold weather, cover your beard with a scarf. This simple step can go a long way in protecting it from the harsh winter elements.
  9. Diet and Nutrition Matter A balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals supports healthy hair growth. Ensure your diet includes plenty of Omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins A, C, E, and Biotin.
  10. Consult with Our Beard Experts At House of Handsome Barbershop, we're more than just barbers; we're beard care experts. If you're experiencing any issues or just need advice on products, don't hesitate to consult with us during your next visit.

Your Winter Beard Care Destination

Remember, a well-cared-for beard is a happy beard, especially during winter. Follow these tips to keep your beard hydrated, healthy, and stylish throughout the season. And for all your beard care needs, House of Handsome Barbershop is your go-to destination. Book your appointment today and let us help you maintain the perfect winter beard.

title: How To Grow A Mullet
content:
Ah, the mullet! A hairstyle that screams retro but has been making a significant comeback in recent years. While some might remember it as the 'business in the front, party in the back' style of the '80s and '90s, today's mullet has evolved to become a fashion-forward choice for the daring gentleman. If you're intrigued and wish to grow a mullet of your own, House of Handsome is here to guide you through every step.

1. Understand the Mullet

Before diving into the growing process, it's essential to understand the mullet's anatomy. Traditionally, a mullet features shorter hair at the front and sides while leaving length at the back.

2. Start with an Even Length

If you're starting from a very short haircut or a buzz cut, give your hair some time to grow to a uniform length. A minimum length of about 2-3 inches will set the stage for a more balanced mullet.

3. Trim the Front and Sides

As your hair grows, you'll want to maintain the front and sides by trimming them regularly. Use scissors for a more natural finish or clippers for a sharper look. However, always leave the back untouched to let it grow.

4. Choose Your Mullet Style

title: Banish Razor Burn: Tips for a Smooth, Irritation-Free Shave
content:
A smooth, clean shave is one of life's small luxuries, but razor burn can quickly turn this pleasurable ritual into a painful experience. Those unsightly red bumps and irritated skin can be a menace. At House of Handsome, we believe every man deserves a perfect shave. So, let's dive into understanding razor burn and, most importantly, how to prevent and treat it.

1. What is Razor Burn?

Razor burn is a skin irritation that occurs shortly after an area has been shaved. It presents as a red rash and can be accompanied by a burning sensation or itchy skin. In more severe cases, razor burn can evolve into razor bumps, where the hair grows backward into the skin, causing painful ingrown hairs.

2. Prevention: The Best Cure

Prep Your Skin: Always cleanse your face with warm water and a gentle facial cleanser. This softens the hair and opens the pores, preparing your skin for a smoother shave. Use a Quality Shaving Cream: A good shaving cream provides a protective barrier between the razor and your skin, reducing friction. Sharp Blades are Essential: Dull blades tug and pull at the hairs instead of cutting cleanly through them, increasing the chances of irritation. Ensure you regularly change your razor blades. Shave in the Right Direction: Always shave in the direction of hair growth. For most men, this means shaving downward on the cheeks and upward on the neck. Aftercare: Post-shave, rinse your face with cold water to close the pores. Apply a hydrating, alcohol-free aftershave or moisturizer to soothe the skin.

3. Treating Razor Burn

If you do experience razor burn, here's how to treat it: Aloe Vera: This natural remedy is known for its soothing properties. Apply aloe vera gel directly to the irritated area to reduce redness and calm inflammation. Witch Hazel: A natural astringent, witch hazel can reduce inflammation and prevent further irritation. Cold Compress: Applying a cold compress can help reduce swelling and soothe burning sensations. Over-the-counter Creams: Look for creams containing hydrocortisone. They can help reduce inflammation and soothe the skin.

4. House of Handsome's Ultimate Solution

Still struggling with razor burn? Perhaps it's time to let the professionals handle your shave. At House of Handsome, we provide expert shaving services using top-of-the-line products and techniques. Our skilled barbers know how to give you a close shave without the burn, ensuring you walk out feeling fresh and irritation-free. Book an appointment today for a professional hot shave.

title: 5 Common Mistakes That Damage Your Beard
content:
Beards have been a sign of masculinity for ages, and for good reason - a well-groomed beard can really enhance your look. But, like any hairstyle, it requires regular maintenance to keep it looking its best. Unfortunately, there are some common mistakes that many men make when it comes to beard care, which can lead to damaged, unruly, and unappealing facial hair. Here are the top five mistakes you need to avoid to keep your beard in top shape:

1. Overwashing

While it's important to keep your beard clean, overwashing it can strip it of its natural oils, leaving it dry, flaky, and brittle. It's best to wash your beard no more than two or three times a week, using a mild shampoo or beard wash specifically designed for facial hair.

2. Not Moisturizing

Just like the hair on your head, your beard needs moisture to stay healthy and soft. After washing, be sure to apply a beard oil or balm to hydrate and nourish the hair and skin underneath. This will also help prevent itching and beard dandruff.

3. Neglecting The Skin Underneath

The skin underneath your beard can also become dry and itchy if not properly cared for. Use a moisturizer or beard oil that is designed to nourish both the hair and skin to keep the area healthy and free from irritation.

4. Using The Wrong Tools

Regular trimming and shaping are essential for maintaining a neat and tidy beard, but using the wrong tools can actually cause damage. Avoid using scissors or clippers designed for your head hair, as they can be too harsh on delicate facial hair. Instead, invest in a high-quality beard trimmer specifically designed for facial hair.

5. Failing To Maintain The Same Length

While it may be tempting to let your beard grow wild and free, failing to maintain the same length can lead to an unkempt, uneven appearance. Regular trimming and shaping will help keep your beard looking well-groomed and tidy.By avoiding these common mistakes, you can ensure that your beard stays healthy, soft, and stylish. If you're unsure about how to properly care for your beard, or if you're in need of a trim or shaping, book an appointment with one of our experienced House of Handsome barbers. We can help your beard become the envy of all your friends with the right care and attention.

However, cultivating a great beard doesn't just happen overnight; it takes consistent care and proper grooming practices. At House of Handsome Barbershop, we understand the importance of a well-maintained beard, and we're here to share some expert tips and tricks for achieving and maintaining a handsome beard.

1. Cleanse Regularly

Just like the hair on your head, your beard needs regular cleansing. Using a good quality beard shampoo will help remove any dirt, sweat, and excess oils, keeping your beard clean, fresh, and smelling great. We recommend washing your beard 2-3 times a week, depending on your lifestyle and skin type.

2. Hydrate and Condition

A dry and brittle beard is neither comfortable nor attractive. After washing, always use a beard conditioner to restore moisture and keep your beard soft and manageable. Additionally, regularly apply beard oil. Not only does it hydrate and nourish your beard, but it also moisturizes the skin underneath, reducing flakiness and itching.

3. Trim for Shape and Health

Even if you're growing your beard out, occasional trimming is beneficial. It helps maintain your beard's shape and removes split ends, which can cause your beard to look frizzy and unkempt. Whether you prefer a minimalist, sculpted, or full-grown beard, we at House of Handsome offer professional trimming services tailored to your desired style.

4. Brush and Comb

Brushing or combing your beard daily helps distribute natural oils throughout your beard, ensuring it stays well-nourished and healthy. It also helps to tame the beard, keeping it neat and styled throughout the day. Remember, always use a wide-toothed comb or a brush designed specifically for beards.

5. Feed Your Beard

A healthy beard starts from the inside out. Hydrate adequately and maintain a balanced diet rich in vitamins like biotin and vitamin E, known to promote hair growth and health. Regular exercise also enhances blood circulation, contributing to healthier, fuller beard growth.

6. Patience is a Virtue

Every beard is unique, and growth rates vary from person to person. Don't be discouraged if your beard growth seems slower than others. Be patient, keep up with your beard care routine, and soon enough, you'll have the handsome beard you aspire to.Caring for your beard is a journey, not a destination. At House of Handsome, we are here to guide and assist you on this journey, providing products, services, and advice that cater specifically to your beard care needs. With our tips and tricks, coupled with a little patience and consistency on your part, you can achieve a handsome beard that complements your personal style and face shape. So gentlemen, embrace the art of beard care today. Book an appointment at House of Handsome Barbershop for personalized care and let your beard do the talking!

title: 5 Habits Every Man Should Follow for Healthy Hair
content:
As men, we often focus on keeping our beard well-groomed but what about our hair? The secret to healthy and lustrous hair is not just about using the right products, it's also about adopting healthy habits. Here are five habits for healthy hair that every man should know:

1. Cold Showers When Washing Your Hair:

Cold Showers When Washing Your Hair: While hot water may feel great on your skin, it's not the best for your hair. Hot water can strip the natural oils from your scalp, leaving your hair dry and brittle. Instead, opt for a cool or cold shower when washing your hair. The cold water helps to seal the cuticles, locking in moisture and leaving your hair looking shiny and healthy.

2. Using Professional Hair Products:

Invest in high-quality, professional hair products that are formulated for your hair type. These products are designed to nourish and protect your hair, keeping it healthy and strong.

3. Using A Microfibre Towel To Dry Your Hair:

Traditional towels can be rough on your hair, causing damage and breakage. Instead, use a microfibre towel to dry your hair. These towels are gentle on your hair, helping to prevent breakage and frizz.

4. Limit Hat Use:

Hats can be a great accessory, but wearing them too often can be damaging to your hair. Tight-fitting hats can cause friction, leading to breakage and split ends. If you must wear a hat, choose a loose-fitting style that won't rub against your hair.

5. Keep Your Hair Hydrated:

Just like your body needs water to stay hydrated, your hair needs moisture to stay healthy. Make sure to drink plenty of water and use a high-quality conditioner to keep your hair hydrated and nourished. A leave-in conditioner can also help to protect your hair from damage and keep it looking shiny and healthy.At House of Handsome, we believe that healthy hair is about more than just grooming. It's about adopting healthy habits that promote strong, healthy hair. Incorporate these five habits into your daily routine, and watch your hair transform from dull and lifeless to shiny and healthy. Make an appointment today with one of our expert barbers today to create your personalized hair care routine.

title: Want To Get Your Hair Coloured? Here Are 4 Key Tips:
content:
Getting your hair dyed can be terrifying whether it's your first time or hundredth. From getting the hair colour right to maintenance, we got you sorted with the top tips to keep your dye looking its best.

Evaluate the whole situation

Depending on the colour you choose, and the type of dye you are using, maintenance can vary significantly. The first thing we would recommend doing is evaluating whether or not you are ready for the level of maintenance required for your specific job. Take some time to do some research into what types of dyes would be best for your hairstyle and how often you will need to treat it. 

Having your dye touched up can start adding up so if you feel like getting regular touch-ups is not within your budget, we would recommend picking a hair colour that is closer to your natural shade so you can get away with less frequent colouring.

Bring pictures with you

It might seem like a simple trick but bringing pictures with you can really help point the hair stylist in the right direction. At House of Handsome, we always encourage you to bring pictures in with you so we can get the most accurate look. Telling the stylist you want “Eminem blonde” could get you his signature dirty blonde look from his early career, or that plain phase he went through in the 2010s. Bringing a picture can eliminate this whole confusion and ensure everyone is on the same page.

Keep in mind your skin tones and natural hair colour

A very common mistake that people make is finding a hair colour they like on a model that looks nothing like them. Skin tones play a huge role in how a hair colour will look on an individual. Brad Pitt’s dirty blonde look might seem like a great idea but try googling images of people with a similar skin tone rocking the same hair colour. Take a look and think to yourself whether or not it would look good on you too. Oftentimes you might find yourself playing around with different styles before landing on the one you love. It's better to make that mistake on photoshop then on your real hair first.

Colouring your hair can damage it

Dyeing your hair is strenuous on the hair follicles and its overall health. Many hair stylists will recommend you do more extensive transformations in multiple steps. This will allow the follicles to heal between sessions and ensure the healthiest look possible. After you've done all your research and landed on a colour you love, come see one of our experienced hair stylists at House of Handsome. title: 5 Haircare Tips for Men From Your Local Barbershop
content:

Not only will it keep you looking your best, but it can improve your concentration and your motivation too.  At House of Handsome, we have compiled our top 5 hair care tips for men. 1. Keep your scalp clean, but not too clean

Shampooing regularly can help keep dangerous bacteria from growing on your scalp. Some of the more common bacteria can inhibit healthy oils and block new follicles from growing causing male pattern baldness.  On the flip side, shampooing too regularly can diminish some of the natural oils in your hair and cause the exact same side effects as never shampooing. The key here is to find a balance that allows you to shampoo less frequently without letting your hair get too oily between washes.

2. Invest in the right products

While there are a ton of products out there that can be gimmicky and claim to provide certain benefits, there are others that really do what they say they do. The best way to weed out the good ones from the bad is to consult your dermatologist or family doctor to see what types of products will be best for your hair.

3. Have a routine oiling day

Oiling your hair is more common in eastern parts of the world but has begun to see an emergence in the west. While there are no studies to show whether it positively impacts hair growth, it is unanimously seen as a positive thing to do once in a while to maintain moisture and promote a healthy scalp. Pick a day of the month when you can leave the oil in your hair for at least an hour and commit to it. Your hair will thank you in the long run!

4. Use Conditioner

That bottle your mom/sister/wife leaves inside the shower that you have never touched is a good one! Your first instinct might tell you that it's only for girls with longer hair, but believe us when we say this could possibly change your hair for the better. Many men will steer clear of conditioner, but those of us who have learned to use it regularly will vouch for it any day. Give it a try and be consistent! You’ll see positive changes in no time.

5. Visit your barber regularly

Having your hair cut is not only great for your appearance and your confidence, but also for the overall health of your hair. As your hair is exposed the elements it will build up minor fractures and begin to tear near the end. These split ends and minor forms of breakage may not seem like a big deal but having the tips trimmed off can reinvigorate your entire head. Even if you are trying to grow your hair out, having the tips trimmed can promote healthy growth and keep you feeling your best. title: Dandruff relief? Here Are Some Tips From A Master Barber In Edmonton.
content:
Dandruff can be a pesky problem and there is a good chance that you may have to deal with it at some point. Some cases are worse than others, but the good news is that dandruff can be treated fairly simply by yourself. Only in extreme cases will you need to see a dermatologist, but for the most part it boils down to your overall scalp health.  Dandruff is caused by a fungus called Malassezia which is naturally occurring on the human scalp, but in large quantities can cause the dead skin to flake off in excess. Malassezia overgrowth is caused by many factors, including stress, hormones, and age.  Here are some tips on how to control dandruff from a master barber at House of Handsome in Edmonton:

Watch Your Diet

What you choose to eat has many effects on your physical, and mental health. You can almost entirely resolve most minor health-related issues by adjusting your diet a little bit. Foods with high carb and sugar content result in a buildup of glycogen in your skin and this can directly cause dandruff you are dealing with.

Wash Your Hair More Often

At its essence, dandruff is just flaky skin. It is perfectly normal for all humans to have small amounts of dandruff at all times. Washing your hair more often simply clears that outer layer of dandruff that may be stuck inside those luscious curls. It can also prompt your scalp to begin replenishing the oils you lost while shampooing, therefore moisturizing your scalp. Just be careful not to shampoo too often otherwise you may dry out your scalp too much.

Use A Special Dandruff Shampoo

As gimmicky as it may sound, dandruff shampoo is a thing that works! Dandruff shampoo contains zinc and sulfur which actively prevents the growth of fungus. It's a simple solution and works most of the time, but you can always speak to a dermatologist to get recommendations on dandruff shampoos that will work best for your skin.

Don't Scratch

This is probably the most difficult tip because we all know that there are few things more satisfying than scratching that pesky itch out of your head. Having an itchy head is the first sign that you have dandruff beginning to flake off. Your first instinct will always be to scratch it but if you can manage to hold off long enough to take a shower or treat it with tea tree oil, you may save yourself from inflammation or infection. At House of Handsome, we hope that these tips help your scalp feel its best. Dandruff is tricky but it is more annoying than it is dangerous (in most cases). Try these tips next time your dandruff flares, and we would love to hear how they helped you on your journey to having a healthier scalp.

title: How To Shave, Trim, And Shape Your Own Beard
content:
Having your beard done at the barber is one of the sweet joys of masculine self-care. When your beard is done right, it can feel like the confidence boost lasts weeks. The barber will make it look easy, but the truth is, it can be! Getting it right might take a few tries but here is a step-by-step guide on how to shave, trim, and shape your own beard.

Step 1: Keep Your Beard Clean And Well Maintained

Believe it or not, the best thing you can do to trim your beard takes place well before you even pick up the clippers. Beards are an unruly mess sometimes and having yours well maintained and kept clean can really make a world of a difference. There is a reason when you have your beard done at the barbers that they will spray it with water and comb it down. Keeping those strays under control means you will have a more even cut. Using beard scrubs and oils regularly can keep your beard in a tame shape so it's always ready for a fresh shape-up.

Step 2: Brush Brush Brush

As we mentioned above, your barber will brush your beard to keep the strays from making the cut uneven. Many people who trim their beards on their own will forget this step but it is so important! Your beard has a natural flow and if you let your comb do the hard work, you'll have a better idea of where to trim and aim those lines. We recommend using a brush for bushier beards, but for the finer areas like the mustache and sideburns, you definitely want to use a comb.

Step 3: Time To Trim

You definitely want to start with the clippers here. Set your desired length and make sure your battery is charged if you're using a rechargeable set. The last thing you want is dead clippers halfway through the trim. Now that you're all set, it’s time to begin. You are most likely going to use multiple clipper sizes, so have them all out and ready. Start with the longest length and trim downwards towards your chin all around. Use any of the smaller sizes to fine-tune the shorter areas.

Step 4: Mustache

Now that everything is roughly the same length, you’re ready to begin the mustache. For this part, you want to use scissors if possible. Use a comb to pull the hairs down and trim away any excess that may be covering your lips. When you're done, you can use a razor to get the really tight areas at the top of your lips and close to the nose. We recommend a straight razor if you feel comfortable using one!

Step 5: Define Your Neckline

Since you already have the razor in your hand, it’s time to start creating a neckline. The most common mistake we see people make is following the jawline, not the neckline. Your beard is meant to extend down your neck a little. You obviously don't want to have one of those deep neckbeards, so try to find a middle ground here. Most people like it to extend down to the adam's apple, but play around with different styles and see what suits you best!Now that your beard is done, the last step is to finish with some oil and aftershave. Using aftershave will soothe the skin and leave you feeling and smelling fresh. Top it off with some oil for softness and you're ready to show off that fresh new trim. Practice makes perfect, but for those who prefer a more experienced touch, House of Handsome would love to help you look your best!

title: Different Fade Styles & Which One Suits Your Hair Best
content:
It might come as a news flash to some, but there are indeed different types of fades. This revelation is a hidden secret of the barbershop world and like the secret menu at McDonalds, you just need to know what to order. Here is our guide to picking the right fade for you.

What Is A Fade?

To start, we need to first understand what a fade is. While some barbers do it better than others, a good fade will blend the sides of your head so that the skin and the hair seamlessly transition into one cohesive hairstyle. A good fade is hard to come by, so talk to your barber at House of Handsome to see if a fade will work with your haircut of choice.

Low Fade Vs High Fade

Having curly hair is often a blessing and a curse. While it is envied by anyone with straight hair, they often don't realize how much effort it takes to maintain. For that reason, we recommend using something with a little more hold. Pomades are a great option for people with curly hair because they will also add a necessary shine that gets better throughout the day. A little bit of American Crew Pomade can really make those curls stand out in the most classic way. Try slicking your hair back with it in the morning and watch those curls bloom by the time you leave the house.

Fade Level

Once you have decided whether you like it low or high, you just need to decide your fade level. The fade level refers to the starting point shave level. For example, if you picked a low fade, you may want to choose a 0.5 or 0 for the starting point. This means your hair will fade from nothing (or close to it) into whatever haircut you have chosen for the top. Typically low fades will have a lower fade level, while high fades will have a higher one. Feel free to get creative though!Choosing your hairstyle is hard enough! Telling the barber what you want is a whole new beast. We hope that this guide helps you feel more confident when telling your barber exactly what you're looking for. Get your haircut with confidence at House of Handsome and drop in for your next fade - low or high.

title: Mens Waxing Guide To Look Super Clean For Your Significant Other
content:
For many men, waxing can be an incredibly scary thought and could bring back memories of Steve Carell screaming in pain during his famous waxing scene in The 40-year Old Virgin. Are you thinking about waxing unwanted hairs for a special occasion? Check out our top tips from the experts at House of Handsome in Spruce Grove & Sherwood Park.

1. Hair Length Is Key

Making sure the hair length is right seems counterintuitive to removing hair, but it is essential in allowing the hairs to properly adhere to the strip. The American Academy of Dermatology recommends waxing hairs that are between one-fourth to three-fourths an inch in length.  Waxing hairs that are too short or too long can cause unwanted irritation to the skin. Nothing is going to ease the slight sting you feel when the wax strip is pulled off, but you can prevent your skin from being irritated for several weeks by simply trimming the hair to its appropriate length.

2. Exfoliate Your Skin

We recommend doing this two days before your waxing appointment. You can book an appointment here, but make sure to allow yourself two days in advance to exfoliate your skin. This key step removes impurities and can give you a cleaner waxing job. The reason we recommend doing it two days before is so the skin is not too sensitive from the substances in most exfoliators.

3. Avoid Retinoids On Waxing Day

Retinoids are a great way to thicken your skin and reduce signs of aging. Many anti-aging creams contain this chemical which can make the waxing significantly more difficult. While there is no harm in using anti-aging lotion, we recommend you refrain from using them up to 48 hours before your appointment.

4. Take A Pain Killer Before You Go

We know, it's the same advice your mom would give you, but it works! Couple of hours before your appointment, take an over-the-counter pain killer to reduce the amount of pain your skill will feel. This can bring waxing pains from a 10/10 down to a 7/10 depending on your tolerance to painkillers.  Obviously, we recommend speaking to your doctor to determine the dosage and brand you want to take.

5. Reduce Discomfort With Cold Packs

The sting peaks immediately and then quickly starts feeling better. While the initial pull is the worst of it, you can apply an ice pack to reduce the amount of inflammation and blood flow on affected areas. Using an ice pack is one of the quickest ways to reduce the pain and it's a solution that is as old as the method itself! At House of Handsome, we are here to give you the best experience, whether it's your first time or your hundredth. Your comfort and experience are our primary concern and we take steps to ensure you feel as little pain as possible when getting waxed on any part of your body.

title: Upcoming Hairstyles to Look Out for in 2022
content:
With a new year comes new hairstyles. 2021 was a great time for experimenting with hairstyles as the pandemic allowed for more freedom of expression as offices and businesses were closed or operating from home. Having fresh ideas and fresh resolutions for the coming year is great, but we wanted to talk about some fresh men’s hairstyles to look out for in 2022.

Mullet

Believe it or not, the mullet is making a comeback. The classic saying of “Business in the front, party in the back” has never been more applicable. As zoom meetings provide a two-dimensional playing field, the mullet is one of our top picks for fresh hairstyles of 2022.  The mullet stands out and can scream confidence and here at House of Handsome, we are beyond excited to see how you decide to style yours.

Buzz Cut

Short hairstyles have, and always will be fresh. The Buzz Cut is a classic that seems to have reemerged as gender-fluid hairstyles emerge into the mainstream. Many folks have put a twist on the classic by adding unique colours or fading into a buzz cut. Regardless of how you decide to add a modern twist to this classic, you really can't go wrong with a good old buzz cut.  A good buzz cut is also a great way to fade into your beard, giving you a clean and low-maintenance look that you can wear at parties just as well as you would in a meeting. Don't sleep on the buzz cut in 2022!

Curls

For the folks looking for a more natural look, there is no shortage of options available to you with minimal effort.  Sometimes the best way to manage curls is not to. There are so many ways you can style your curls and you can be as professional or shaggy as you like. Whether you're going for a modern chiseled Harry Styles look or a classic shaggy David Bowie, it's time to embrace your curls and gain an appreciation for the versatility they offer.
